transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-10-06
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Devon Rivera (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (Redwood CSM); Lena Singh (Starlit CTO), Arjun Patel (Lead Backend), Priya Nair (Head of Security), Mika Torres (Product)

Topics: quickstart credits, reserved pilot (dedicated capacity), security/KMS, SSO/SAML, latency vs cost, benchmark plan, rollout timeline.

[00:00] Ethan (AE): "All right, thanks everyone for jumping on. I'm Ethan, I'm the AE on this account. We'll do a quick intro round then Devon will go into the infra and perf bits. Um, goal for today is to figure out whether you want to start with our self-serve quickstart with credits or formalize a reserved pilot — figure out success criteria and next steps."

[00:22] Lena S (CTO): "Thanks, Ethan. I'm Lena, CTO at Starlit. We ingest a lot of time-series telemetry and want LLM features for alert summarization and root cause suggestions. Key constraints: PII avoidance, on-prem forwarding for sensitive payloads, and predictable latency under 300ms tail for the critical path. We're evaluating hosted vs reserved/dedicated because of cost predictability and compliance."

[00:45] Arjun (Lead Backend): "Yeah hi, I'm Arjun. Current stack: services on AWS EKS, some inference on batch GPUs internally but it's pretty brittle. Prefer something that can do streaming responses and also support batching for cheaper non-latency paths. We'll probably start with a single endpoint for summaries then expand to reranker later."

[01:10] Devon (SE): "Great. Quick overview — Redwood has the hosted Redwood API (fast to start), Reserved pools (dedicated capacity for pilots/production), and Private deployments for VPC/on-prem. For quickstart we can issue credits, you self-serve and hit the hosted API right away. For reserved pilot we reserve GPU pools with SLA targets and predictable throughput. The tradeoffs: hosted gives fastest time-to-first-request, reserved gives guaranteed throughput and can reduce unit cost at scale."

[01:46] Priya (Security): "Quick question: SOC2 is table stakes, but we also need KMS integration — customer-managed keys — and audit logs available in a retention window of at least 12 months. Also SSO, SAML works?"

[02:05] Devon: "Yes — we support SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS support in Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and customer KMS for Private deployments; there are some managed options for hosted with BYOK in select regions. Audit logs and retention policy can be configured — default is 90 days for hosted, but enterprise add-ons extend that."

[02:40] Mika (Product): "What's the usual time-to-first-request if we go self-serve? Like, how fast can my PM get a prototype?"

[02:50] Ethan: "Usually minutes to a working call — with our quickstart docs and SDK. Realistically you can have a token and send requests within a day; to get meaningful integrated results it's usually a few days once you have prompts and sample inputs. We do provide a starter repo and step-by-step guide: https://redwood.ai/quickstart — I'll include the link."

[03:20] Lena S: "And for the reserved pilot, how long to stand up capacity? We don't want a months-long procurement cycle."

[03:28] Devon: "A reserved pilot (we call it Reserved) typically takes 1–2 weeks for provisioning after contract signed if it's hosted reserved capacity. Private/on-prem can be longer. We have standard pilot templates to reduce setup friction. If you want a VPC Private, plan for 3–6 weeks depending on networking and firewall approvals."

[03:55] Arjun: "Can you talk about latency numbers? We need tail latency under ~300ms for 512 token sequences ideally."

[04:05] Devon: "For smaller open models with optimized kernels and streaming, median is often sub-100ms for short sequences; 95/99th depends on load and batching. With Dedicated reserved pools and KV/prefix caching you can hit consistent tails. We'll want to run a benchmark with your payloads — that will show realistic numbers. I note that sequence length, batch behavior, and KV cache usage drastically shift tail latency."

[04:40] Priya: "How do you handle PII? We want to make sure no sensitive logs are stored in cleartext in hosted logs."

[04:50] Devon: "We have optional request redaction, prefix/KV caching controls, and can configure not to persist payloads for hosted trial. For full compliance we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS so raw payloads never leave your VPC or are encrypted at rest with your keys."

[05:12] Speaker 1 (unknown): "And is the KV cache per-tenant or globally shared?"

[05:20] Devon: "Per tenant within a pool. For Reserved pools it's isolated, and for Private it's customer-controlled. Hosted pools may have multi-tenant nodes but with strong tenant isolation — but yes, for strict separation you do Reserved/Dedicated or Private."

[05:45] Lena S: "What's pricing like for Reserved? We're a mid-stage company, so a full dedicated cluster is too big. We were thinking of a small reserved pilot for 2-3 months to validate unit economics."

[06:00] Ethan: "Reserved pilots often start with a 3-month commitment for a small pool. Pricing depends on GPU type and committed throughput; I can send a template. We also offer credits that apply to hosted usage so you can compare run rate. E.g., we can provision $10k of trial credits on hosted to run initial PoC and then if you like we move to Reserved pilot pricing based on observed RPS and token consumption."

[06:30] Arjun: "If we do hosted quickstart with credits and then switch to Reserved, how seamless is model and API compatibility?"

[06:40] Devon: "We keep the same API across modes. You can pin model versions and use rollout policies. The routing layer will migrate requests to reserved pools; there may be footprint differences if you choose a quantized variant, but code-level changes are minimal."

[07:05] Mika: "Any limitations on function-calling or streaming with hosted vs reserved?"

[07:12] Devon: "No, streaming and function/tool-calling are supported across all modes. The main difference is SLOs and capacity guarantees for Reserved. For heavy real-time streaming you might prefer Reserved to ensure burst handling."

[07:30] Priya: "About data residency: some of our customers require EU-only storage. Do you have region controls?"

[07:36] Ethan: "Yes region controls are supported. Hosted offers region selection; Reserved and Private give you more control. We'll share our data residency doc and the list of regions we offer."

[07:50] Mika: "Okay, can you outline a suggested pilot plan?"

[07:55] Ethan: "Proposed: Phase 1 (0-2 weeks) — Quickstart with hosted credits, onboard PMs, prototype endpoint using your sample dataset, measure baseline latency and quality. Phase 2 (week 2-4) — run a benchmark with SE pair, test 95/99 latencies, model variants, batching. Phase 3 (month 1) — decide Reserved pilot if economics and latencies look good, sign short reserved pilot (3 months) and migrate traffic. That's flexible though."

[08:30] Arjun: "If we run benchmarks, what do you need from us?"

[08:32] Devon: "Sample corpus (~5k-15k documents), expected RPS, typical prompt lengths, and a list of success metrics — e.g., 95th <=300ms, cost per 1k tokens under $X, and quality thresholds — we'll run realistic load tests and share traces. Also any auth/ingress constraints for Private testing."

[09:00] Priya: "From security side, we'll need the standard security questionnaire filled and a pointer to KMS options. Also attestations around data deletion and a list of sub-processors."

[09:15] Devon: "I'll upload the security pack. For hosted we provide a sub-processor list and data deletion policies; for Reserved/Private you have stronger controls and can get additional contractual clauses."

[09:35] Lena S: "One concern: our cost team is sensitive to per-token costs. How do batching and quantization affect that?"

[09:44] Devon: "Batching reduces per-token costs when latency SLOs allow it; quantized variants reduce memory and compute costs, sometimes at small quality tradeoffs. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching/quant profiles per workload. As part of the pilot we'll recommend a quantized model family if it meets your quality bar to lower unit economics."

[10:10] Mika: "Any pitfalls teams usually hit when moving from quickstart to reserved?"

[10:15] Ethan: "Common ones: not having representative load tests (so the reserved sizing is off), skip of SSO setup early which slows integration, and not locking down logging/retention requirements prior to pilot. We try to surface these early."

[10:32] Arjun: "Licensing/legal — how quickly can procurement sign off? Do you have a standard pilot agreement?"

[10:40] Ethan: "We have a standard pilot template for Reserved that most customers sign quickly; it's lean for trials. We'll send it with pricing; legal typically turns it in 1-2 weeks for smaller deals."

[11:02] Priya: "Can you confirm encryption at rest details? Hosted vs Reserved?"

[11:08] Devon: "Hosted uses platform-managed keys by default, customer keys via envelope encryption in select regions; Reserved can be configured with customer-managed keys depending on plan, and Private is full BYOK/HSM options. I'll link the KMS faq."

[11:28] (Crosstalk) Lena M (CSM): "I'll make sure we get the credits provisioned right after this call. Ethan, you'll send the pricing?"

[11:35] Ethan: "Yes, I'll email the pricing and pilot template. Devon I'll defer the SOC2 and KMS links to you to attach."

[11:45] Arjun: "Quick technical: do you support streaming multiple responses (N-best) and then reranking server-side?"

[11:52] Devon: "Yes, we support n-best/beam-style outputs and reranking. You can also run a reranker model in the same pool. We'll want to measure cost for the multi-pass strategy."

[12:10] Priya: "About logs — will audit logs include token-level traces?"

[12:17] Devon: "Audit logs capture request metadata and trace ids; token-level access logs are restricted but available under enterprise add-ons and with contractual constraints. We can provide sample log schemas."

[12:40] Mika: "OK, sounds good. Any references or docs we should read first?"

[12:45] Ethan: "I'll send the quickstart link, pilot template, and security whitepaper after the call. Links: https://redwood.ai/quickstart, https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper.pdf, and the reserved pilot FAQ https://redwood.ai/reserved-pilot-faq"

[13:05] Lena S: "Timeline — we want a pilot started before our next board meeting in late October. Is that feasible?"

[13:12] Ethan: "If we get a signed pilot by Oct 10, yes, we can provision and run initial benchmarks by Oct 20. So timeline looks tight but doable."

[13:30] Devon: "One more note: when we run benchmarks, we'll instrument token-level latency distributions and KV cache hit rates — those are often the big levers for tail reduction. We'll include recommendations for batch window tuning."

[13:50] Arjun: "Regarding cost: if we go Reserved after trial, can credits roll into the pilot commitment?"

[13:56] Ethan: "Usually credits can be applied up to a negotiated point; we'll show the math in the pricing worksheet so you can compare run-rate vs trial adjusted cost."

[14:10] Priya: "We may also require a short technical deep dive with your infra folks about network egress and peering for Private. Can we schedule that?"

[14:18] Devon: "Absolutely — let's plan a 60–90 minute technical deep dive after we get the questionnaire answers. I and our infra lead can join."

[14:35] Lena S: "Ok let's summarize next steps."

[14:40] Ethan: "Recap: Redwood will provision hosted trial credits and share quickstart link; Devon will upload SOC2 + KMS/security pack; Ethan will send pilot pricing and reserved template; Arjun will provide sample dataset and load expectations; Priya will circulate security questionnaire items. We'll schedule benchmark for week of Oct 11-18. Does that align?"

[15:05] (All) "Yes / sounds good"

[15:12] Ethan: "Great — I'll follow up with an email with links and the proposed dates. Thanks everyone, we'll be in touch."

[15:20] Meeting end.
